title: Question tags (do you? isn't it? etc.)

exercises.instruction: Complete these sentences with a question tag.

answers: will she
aren't you
don't you
were you
does she
isn't he

parts: It didn't take long to get here,
answers: did it
can't you

parts: They won't mind if I take a picture,
answers: will they

parts: There are a lot of people here,
answers: aren't there
shall we
is it
aren't I
would you

parts: Helen has lived here a long time,

exercises.instruction: In these situations you expect your friend to agree with you. Use a question tag in your sentences.

answers: It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
It's (very) expensive, isn't it?
The course was great, wasn't it?
You've had your hair cut, haven't you?
You had your hair cut, didn't you?
She has a good voice, doesn't she?
She has a good voice, hasn't she?
She's got a good voice, hasn't she?
She has got a good voice, hasn't she?
It doesn't look right, does it?
This bridge isn't very safe, is it?
This bridge doesn't look very safe, does it?

exercises.instruction: In these situations you are asking for information, asking people to do things etc.

items.prompt: You need a pen. Perhaps Jane has one. Ask her.
answers: Jane, you don't have a pen I could borrow, do you?

items.prompt: You have to move a heavy table. You want Joe to help you with it. Ask him.
answers: Joe, you couldn't help me (with this table), could you?

items.prompt: You're looking for Sarah. Perhaps Lisa knows where she is. Ask her.
answers: Lisa, you don't know where Sarah is, do you?
Lisa, you haven't seen Sarah, have you?

items.prompt: You want to borrow a tennis racket. Perhaps Helen has one. Ask her.
answers: Helen, you don't have a tennis racket, do you?
Helen, you haven't got a tennis racket, have you?

items.prompt: Anna has a car and you need a lift to the station. Perhaps she'll take you. Ask her.
answers: Anna, you couldn't take me to the station, could you?
Anna, you couldn't give me a lift to the station, could you?

items.prompt: You're looking for your keys. Perhaps Robert has seen them. Ask him.
answers: Robert, you haven't seen my keys, have you?
